label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
**An update from me, and a thank-you I don’t quite have words for yet**

To my friends, family, neighbours, the Little Acorns families, and everyone who has messaged, phoned, prayed, donated, dropped something off or shared a post: thank you. Please feel free to forward this letter to anyone who has been asking about me. I’m writing one proper update because my phone has not stopped since Saturday night, and I simply don’t have the energy to answer everyone individually. I have seen so many of your messages, though, and they mean more than I can explain.

First, and most importantly: **I am safe.** I’m staying with my sister in Rondebosch, and Marmalade, my cat, is safe too. I’m exhausted, emotional and still trying to process everything, but I am being looked after.

Here is the short version of what happened. I’m not going to go through every detail, because I’m not ready to keep reliving it.

At about 11:40pm on Saturday, 7 November, a fire started in a ground-floor flat at Lindale Court on Station Road in Observatory. I live on the second floor, in flat 12. There are 14 flats in the building. Everyone got out. Two people were treated for smoke inhalation at Groote Schuur and were sent home afterwards.

I woke up because my neighbour, Uncle Faizel, was banging on every door on our floor in his vest and slippers. I will never be able to thank him properly for that. I grabbed my phone and Marmalade, and nothing else. Poor Marmalade then hid under a car for two hours afterwards, so she has also had quite enough excitement for one lifetime.

The fire department has said the fire was probably caused by an electrical fault, but it is still being investigated. I’m not going to speculate beyond that.

My flat is not somewhere I can live right now. There is smoke and water damage everywhere, and the lounge ceiling came down. My landlord has said that nobody will be allowed back into the building for at least six weeks. I don’t yet know exactly what, if anything, I’ll be able to recover. At the moment I’m taking it one phone call and one day at a time.

I keep coming back to this: furniture can be replaced. Marmalade can’t. People can’t. Everyone getting out is the thing that matters most.

I have been completely overwhelmed by people’s kindness. One of my Little Acorns moms left a bag of clothes at my sister’s gate at 7am on Sunday without even knocking. She just left it there for me. People have offered beds, clothes, lifts, meals, money, phone calls and practical help. Neighbours who were standing outside in the middle of the night, having lost who knows what themselves, were still checking on one another. I’ve cried at so many of your messages that I’ve lost count.

I also want to say something honestly: I hate asking for help. I feel very strange about having a fundraiser in my name. My friend Zinhle set one up, and when I started feeling awkward about it, she told me to shut up and accept it. So I’m trying to listen to her.

**Zinhle’s official BackaBuddy page is:**

**backabuddy.example/thandi-lindale-court**

The target is **R25 000**, mainly to help me with the deposit and initial costs of getting into a new place, and with replacing essential work items. When Zinhle checked this morning, it was already at **R11 400**. That number made me cry too. Thank you to every single person who has donated or shared it. Please don’t feel that a small contribution doesn’t matter. It does, and so does sharing the page with someone else.

**Please also read this part carefully, because there is another “fund” going around that is not ours.**

I have been sent links to a page calling itself **“Thandi Fire Relief”**, as well as a WhatsApp message asking people to make an EFT into a Capitec account. **Neither of these is connected to me, Zinhle or our fundraiser. Please do not donate through that page or send money to that account.** I have reported it.

The BackaBuddy link above is the official fundraiser. If you receive a different link or banking details and you’re unsure, please check with me or Zinhle before sending anything. I hate that we even have to include a warning like this while people are trying to help, but I don’t want anyone’s kindness to be taken advantage of.

For anyone who has asked what would genuinely help, these are the things I need most right now:

- **Help towards the deposit and moving costs for a new place**, through the official BackaBuddy page.
- **Work clothes and school shoes.** I wear size 34 clothing and size 6 shoes. Comfortable, practical clothes for teaching are especially useful.
- **A laptop, if anyone has an older one that still works properly.** All my lesson planning was on my laptop, and replacing that side of my work life is going to be difficult without one.

And these are the things I **don’t** need at the moment, much as I appreciate the thought:

- **No more general clothing donations, please.** I have already received more than I can use, and I’ll pass suitable extras on to people from the other flats.
- **No food for now, please.** My sister’s freezer is full, and we genuinely don’t have space for more.

If you were planning to drop something off, please rather message first so we don’t duplicate things or create more sorting and storing for my sister. That is not me being ungrateful. I’m just trying to keep the help manageable and make sure it goes where it’s needed.

To my **Little Acorns Pre-Primary parents**, especially my Ladybirds families: I know some of you have heard about the concert things that were in my flat. All the things I had taken home to laminate for the end-of-year concert are gone, including the 22 crowns and the children’s handprint banner. I was very sad about that, because I knew how much work and excitement had gone into them.

But please don’t worry: **the concert on 27 November is still happening, and the Ladybirds will have crowns.** We’ll make a plan. It may not look exactly like the plan I had before, but the children will still have their special day.

I’ll be back at school on Wednesday. My one request is please not to make a big thing of the fire in front of the children. I want their day to feel normal, safe and familiar. Hugs are welcome; a big emotional scene in front of four- and five-year-olds is probably more than I’ll manage.

Finally, please don’t be offended if I don’t answer a DM, miss your call or take a long time to reply to a comment. I’m not ignoring you. I’m just very tired, and there is a lot to sort out. I’ll reply slowly, when I can. If something is urgent or practical, Zinhle can help make sure it reaches me.

Thank you for holding me up while I try to find my feet again. Thank you for checking on the other residents too, and for remembering that I’m not the only person whose home was affected. I don’t have a neat ending for this yet. I’m just safe, sore-hearted, incredibly grateful, and taking the next step.

With love and so much thanks,  
**Thandi**
